neet_che_u03_t05_1.working: With the same Li+ cation, the largest anion is the most polarisable. I- is largest, so LiI has the maximum covalent character.

neet_che_u03_t05_2.working: Cation charge rises and size falls from Na+ to Mg2+ to Al3+. Polarising power rises in that order, so AlCl3 > MgCl2 > NaCl.

neet_che_u03_t05_3.working: Cu+ has an 18-electron configuration (3d10). The d electrons shield the nucleus poorly, so Cu+ is more polarising than Na+ with its noble gas configuration.

neet_che_u03_t05_4.working: A: Li+ is smaller than Na+, same charge, both noble gas type (II). B: Cu+ has an 18-electron configuration (III). C: I- is larger and more polarisable than F- (I). D: Al3+ carries a higher charge (IV).

neet_che_u03_t05_5.working: A is correct. B is wrong: covalent character decreases water solubility. C is correct: AgCl is less soluble than expected. D is wrong: a larger anion is more polarisable. E is correct.
